prompt:
Continue this exact laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage for 10 seconds. Same camera, viewpoint, lighting, colours, image quality and anatomy as the input image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frame):
A circular laparoscopic view shows the dissection of Calot's triangle. A metallic grasper with a black insulated shaft enters from the top center edge, holding the whitish peritoneal fold near the upper gallbladder wall. The gallbladder occupies the left side, displaying a bluish-grey wall covered in fine red vessels and yellow adipose tissue. To the right is the dark reddish-brown liver lobe with small pale patches and glossy highlights. Below the gallbladder, a dissected window reveals two isolated tubular structures, with a single silver metallic clip fastened around the upper cystic artery. Small traces of dark red blood rest near the clipped vessel and in the lower background recess. No second surgical instrument, electrocautery smoke, or active bleeding is visible in the frame.

One surgical step happens (chosen by a patient world model): A laparoscopic clip applier: a long shaft with two jaws holding one small metal clip comes into view along its shaft (or, if it is already in view, moves to the cystic artery). It closes its jaws across the cystic artery, leaving one small metal clip on it, then opens and withdraws.

Instruments already in view: the grasper. An instrument never changes into another instrument. Before the clipper arrives, any instrument in its way slides straight back out of view along its own shaft; the others stay where they are.

By the end of the clip: the cystic artery has 2 small metal clips across it.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands; bleeding; cutting.
explanation: Placing an additional clip on the exposed cystic artery with a complete critical view of safety is a standard step supported by the reference cases (VID22_00473, VID70_00564). Although clipping the artery resolved active bleeding in VID22_00473, bleeding persists in this acutely inflamed patient, and four of the five retrieved transitions indicate that retracting the gallbladder is the most likely next action (VID22_00473, VID70_00557, VID70_00564, VID02_01296).
